perPlanDifferences.value: Daytona publishes one rate card rather than per-tier rates; the tier tables change the resource pool and network access, not the vCPU, memory or storage price. Windows bills a separate OS rate; GPU bills per GPU-hour.
perPlanDifferences.quote: Daytona uses a ... system where organizations are placed into tiers based on verification status, with each tier providing access to a specific compute pool and rate limits.

compute.notes: A container sandbox auto-stops after 15 minutes with no external activity; a background process does not reset the timer. VM sandboxes auto-pause after 60 minutes by default. Neither is a maximum session length.

idle.value: Container sandboxes auto-stop after 15 minutes with no external activity by default; VM sandboxes auto-pause after 60 minutes. A background process does not reset the timer.
idle.quote: if not set, the default interval of 15 minutes is used

billedWhenStopped.value: Yes, disk only. Stopped and paused sandboxes bill reserved disk; CPU and RAM are not billed. Archived container sandboxes and deleted sandboxes bill nothing.
billedWhenStopped.quote: Billed for reserved disk only. The preserved memory state is not billed.

snapshot.value: Snapshots remain billed for storage after the sandbox is deleted, but no separate snapshot rate is published; the only storage rate is $0.000108/GiB-hour.

retention.value: Stopped container sandboxes auto-archive after 7 days by default (30 days is the maximum interval) and stop billing; they are not deleted automatically unless an auto-delete interval or TTL is set. How long archived data is kept is not published.
retention.quote: if not set, the default interval of 7 days is used

snapshotRetention.value: Snapshots become inactive after 2 weeks of not being used; inactivity deactivates rather than deletes.
snapshotRetention.quote: Snapshots automatically become inactive after 2 weeks of not being used.

autoDelete.value: Not set by default: a stopped sandbox is not deleted automatically.
autoDelete.quote: if not set, the sandbox is not deleted automatically

deploy.oneClickOrManaged: Not found. No one-click or managed Hermes/OpenClaw hosting; Daytona supplies the sandbox and the preinstalled binary.
deploy.officialTemplateOrGuide: Yes for OpenClaw: a Daytona guide says OpenClaw is preinstalled in the default snapshot. Hermes is supported as a Hermes terminal backend, not as a Daytona guide.
deploy.manualRoute: OpenClaw: install the Daytona CLI, log in with an API key, run `daytona sandbox create --name openclaw --snapshot daytona-medium --auto-stop 0`, SSH in with `daytona ssh openclaw`, then run OpenClaw onboarding. Hermes: install Hermes on a local machine, set terminal.backend: daytona plus DAYTONA_API_KEY, and Hermes creates and stops/resumes the Daytona sandbox itself.
deploy.nonCoderDashboardOnly: Partly. The dashboard Playground creates a sandbox and opens a web terminal in the browser, so no local install is needed, but the OpenClaw and Hermes setup still requires typed commands and an API key.
